summary: The link handling works: external http/https links and autolinks get target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer", while relative links, anchors, mailto links and images are left alone. But the extension can't be loaded the way the issue asks. `extensions=['external_links']` raises ModuleNotFoundError because the PR adds no entry point to pyproject.toml, which breaks ARCHITECTURE.md constraint 4. The PR's tests don't catch this because they pass an `ExternalLinksExtension()` instance instead of the short name.

own_checks.check: Extension loads by short name: extensions=['external_links'] (issue decision 1)
http/https inline and reference links get target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer
Automatic links <https://...> are marked, including ones with & in the URL
mailto links, automail, #anchors and relative links are unchanged
Default output is unchanged when the extension is not enabled

findings.title: No entry point for external_links, so extensions=['external_links'] fails
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml has no `external_links = 'markdown.extensions.external_links:ExternalLinksExtension'` under [project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions'] (grep for 'external' finds nothing). Running `markdown.markdown('[d](https://e.com)', extensions=['external_links'])` raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'external_links'`. The issue requires loading by this name, and ARCHITECTURE.md constraint 4 says every built-in extension needs an entry point.

findings.title: Tests use the extension class directly, so loading by name is never tested
findings.evidence: Both tests pass `extensions=[ExternalLinksExtension()]`, which is why they pass even though the short name is broken. The tests also don't cover autolinks (`<https://...>`), mailto links, #anchors or images, all of which the maintainer's decisions list explicitly.

notes: The tree processor's priority of 3 fits: it runs after inline (20) and prettify (10) and before unescape (0), and the generated hrefs are already available at that point.
makeExtension has `# pragma: no cover`. Once tests load the extension by string name, that path is exercised, so the pragma can come off.
Consider adding a docs page under docs/extensions/ and listing the extension in the docs index the way the other built-in extensions are.
